title: The research-reproducibility benchmark is defined and its isolated harness is proven
goal: rag.py eval scores a row by an expect_re regex column and gives the frozen benchmark file repro_bench.csv the held-out reword and off-kb checks; benchmarks.py repro sets up three instances, each a working clone outside the checkout whose origin is its own full bare copy of one fixed start commit under _cache/bench-repro/, with the kb MCP server, _cache, the query log and the claims ledger per clone; repro check proves on a probe instance that kbgit.py sync --push lands on the probe's bare copy and never on the real origin; repro run starts the instances' /kb-research sessions at the same time with the same model, prompt, start commit and budget and records each instance's cost, tokens, turns, wall time, model usage and failures; repro compare measures per instance and area the articles and facts added, tag mix, sources, Jaccard overlaps, conflicts, lint and check errors, frozen-set eval results and an agreement figure; one research brief per topic area is committed in repro_briefs.csv; and a frozen set of 3-5 user-style questions per area is committed in repro_bench.csv after the start commit and before any instance runs

gates.question: Approve this sprint's goal and committed items?
